summary:
Goa stands under India's national framework: the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019 and the amendment passed by Parliament on 25 March 2026 operate in this state as in every other state and union territory, and no Goan statute or enforcement pattern diverging from the national position is on file.

Goa has taken one region-specific step under that framework. On 7 May 2025 the state constituted a 14-member Model Transgender Welfare Board, headed by the Chief Secretary, under the 2019 Act and its 2020 Rules, to oversee implementation of welfare schemes and safeguard transgender persons' rights in healthcare, education, employment and housing.

Registration and visibility of trans Goans remain very low. The 2011 Census recorded 398 transgender persons in Goa out of 487,803 nationally. As of 2024 only 12 transgender people were listed on Goan electoral rolls, the first registrations having occurred in 2022.

A 2018 Goa Livelihoods Forum study found that 87% of transgender respondents had dropped out of school because of harassment, an indicator of the social environment a trans visitor may observe.

Same-sex activity was decriminalised nationally in 2018 by Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, and federal law has recognised transgender identity since NALSA v. Union of India in 2014. The 2019 Act prohibits discrimination based on gender identity.

Goa applies the Goa Civil Code, which defines marriage as between a man and a woman; there is no legal recognition for same-sex marriages or civil unions in the state. After the Supreme Court's 2023 decision not to legalise same-sex marriage, activists in Goa urged legislative steps but no bills have been introduced. The Supreme Court noted in 2023 that same-sex couples have the right to cohabit and enjoy some protections under law.

There are currently no state-level anti-discrimination laws protecting sexual orientation in Goa.
tangentialFactors: Goa's colonial-era legal history is severe but historical: the Goa Inquisition criminalised same-sex activity with death by burning and confiscation of property to the Crown, applied in 1528 to a Muslim man and later to a 16-year-old Portuguese army soldier, Alberto Homem. Under the 1568 Constitutions of the Archbishopric of Goa, same-sex activity was classified as a serious sin punishable by deposition from office and lifelong penance for a clergyman and excommunication until repentance for a layman. In 1644 the Tribunal of Goa concluded that female same-sex acts generally did not constitute sodomy but sexual immorality. None of this is current law.
localsOnly:
Residents of Goa access welfare through the 14-member Model Transgender Welfare Board constituted on 7 May 2025, chaired by the Chief Secretary, covering healthcare, education, employment and housing under the 2019 Act and 2020 Rules.

Trans Goans face documented educational exclusion: a 2018 Goa Livelihoods Forum study found 87% of transgender respondents had left school due to harassment. Formal visibility remains minimal, with 12 transgender people on electoral rolls as of 2024 against a 2011 Census count of 398.

There is no state-level anti-discrimination statute protecting sexual orientation in Goa, and no Goan bill on relationship recognition has been introduced following the Supreme Court's 2023 decision.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the Model Transgender Welfare Board has issued any decisions, spending or guidance since its 7 May 2025 constitution is not sourced here; only its formation terms are on file.

No Goan-specific police conduct, detention or airport-screening incidents involving transgender people are documented in this inventory; assessments of police treatment of trans people in the national record are not restated as Goan findings.

The status of the March 2026 amendment at presidential assent is unresolved in these sources; the inventory records passage by both houses and that assent was pending.

Whether the 2011 Census figure of 398 reflects current population is unresolved; no later Goan census count of transgender residents is available.
